transcript.text: Hi Test: Mixed, this is Donna, an AI assistant calling for Alex at Acme (demo). This call is recorded. I saw your work on a Redis-backed rate limiter library. Got a few minutes for a quick screen for the Founding Engineer role?
Great, thanks. Your rate limiter claims 50k requests per second. How did you measure that, and what broke first?
I load tested our Redis limiter with k6 and found the Lua script was the bottleneck, so I switched it to a fixed window counter and we got from about 15k to 50k requests per second on one node.
Nice, moving off the Lua script to a fixed window counter is a clean fix. Quick follow-up: what actually broke first when you shipped that, and how did you find out?
The detail was that each call did a sorted-set trim, which is O(log n) plus the removals, and the fixed window just does one INCR and an EXPIRE.
That explains why it got faster. What actually broke when you shipped it, or what surprised you in production?
For idempotency keys I think you just generate a random UUID on the server for every request and that makes retries safe, it's mostly handled by the database anyway.

If the server generates a new UUID on every request, a client retry gets a new key, so how does the server recognize it as the same payment? What went wrong on the payments team, and how did you find out?
In my first two weeks I'd read the gateway code, set up tracing on the slowest endpoints, and take one small on-call ticket to learn the system.
Tracing the slowest endpoints is a solid plan, and starting with the gateway makes sense. Thanks, Test: Mixed. I'll pass my notes to Alex, and you'll get a calendar invite if they'd like to meet.
Thanks for your time, Test: Mixed. Have a good rest of your day.

elevenLabsAnalysis.transcript_summary:
The agent, Donna, conducted a screening call for a Founding Engineer role, discussing the user's Redis-backed rate limiter. The user explained optimizing it from 15k to 50k RPS by replacing a Lua script with a fixed window counter.

The conversation also touched on idempotency keys, where the agent challenged the user's approach of server-generated UUIDs for retries. Finally, the user outlined their plan for the first two weeks in a new role, focusing on code review, tracing, and on-call tickets. The agent concluded by stating notes would be passed on for potential next steps.
